web-service.title: Scaling a Modern Web Application
web-service.subtitle: System Design Interview: From Simple Monolith to Distributed Async Architecture

steps.name: Single-Server MVP
steps.interviewerPrompt: Let's start with the basics: Design a service where clients can query data and perform updates with low latency.
steps.solution: Establish the synchronous request path: Client sends HTTP requests to a stateless CPU API server, which reads and writes directly to the primary database.
tradeoffs: Single point of failure (SPOF) at the database layer
Read queries compete with write transactions for locks and disk I/O
Zero caching: repeated identical reads hit disk every time

steps.name: Caching & Read Replicas
steps.interviewerPrompt: Our read traffic just surged 10x (90% reads, 10% writes). Database CPU is spiking at 95% and queries are timing out. How do we scale reads?
steps.solution: Introduce an in-memory TTL cache (e.g. Redis) using the Cache-Aside pattern, and split database traffic with asynchronous read replicas.
tradeoffs: Cache invalidation challenges (TTL expiration vs. explicit invalidation)
Replication lag: eventual consistency means clients might read slightly stale data immediately after a write
Cache stampede (dogpiling) when hot keys expire concurrently

steps.name: Asynchronous Task Queue & Workers
steps.interviewerPrompt: Users are triggering heavy background tasks (PDF generation, webhook dispatches, data processing) that take 5 to 30 seconds. API connection pools are exhausting. How do we decouple?
steps.solution: Add an asynchronous leased task queue (e.g. SQS/RabbitMQ) with a dedicated pool of background workers writing to an idempotent results store, plus a dead-letter queue (DLQ) for failed retries.
tradeoffs: Asynchronous response model: clients must poll or subscribe via WebSockets for job completion
Idempotency: workers must handle duplicate delivery safely using unique idempotency keys
Backpressure and poison-pill messages: unhandled tasks must route to DLQ after N retries

chat-application.title: Real-Time Streaming Chat System
chat-application.subtitle: System Design Interview: Persistent Conversations, Inference Pool, and Token Streaming

steps.name: Conversation Persistence
steps.interviewerPrompt: Design the core chat service: User submits prompts, authenticates, and conversation history is reliably saved.
steps.solution: Client connects through an Ingress gateway that validates identity policies, then forwards to the Chat service which persists prompts and history with retry bounds.
tradeoffs: Strict authorization checks on every operation prevent unauthorized access across tenants
Retry policies with bounded attempts avoid cascading failures against database locks
Synchronous HTTP responses are too slow for LLM generation

steps.name: Model Router & Inference Pool
steps.interviewerPrompt: We need to connect LLM workers to generate replies, but different models have different latencies and GPU capacity limits.
steps.solution: Introduce an Admission Controller and Model Router that dispatches generation tasks across worker pools based on availability and quotas.
tradeoffs: GPU capacity is finite; quota admission prevents memory exhaustion on model nodes
Load balancing across diverse model checkpoints with speculative fallback
Need to ensure tokens don't block other waiting users

steps.name: Real-Time Token Streaming
steps.interviewerPrompt: Waiting for full generation takes 10+ seconds. How do we deliver tokens incrementally as they generate, and survive sudden disconnects?
steps.solution: Add a dedicated Streaming Session manager and Delivery pipeline that pushes tokens to clients via WebSockets/SSE while asynchronously committing the completed reply to the conversation store.
tradeoffs: Client reconnection requires stream resumption tokens to avoid missing or duplicated tokens
Decoupled delivery: slow network connections on client side don't stall the GPU worker
Atomic commit of assistant message once generation finishes

rag-assistant.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) System
rag-assistant.subtitle: System Design Interview: From Baseline Model to Vector Retrieval & Reranking Ingestion

steps.name: Baseline LLM Pipeline
steps.interviewerPrompt: Let's build an AI assistant that answers user questions with structured schema validation.
steps.solution: Client questions route through API server to GPU worker pool, then through structured output validation before returning to user.
tradeoffs: Severe hallucinations on private or recent knowledge without external context
Context window limitations if large documents are stuffed into prompt
Model weights are static and cannot reflect daily updates

steps.name: Vector Retrieval (Dense RAG)
steps.interviewerPrompt: We need the assistant to cite internal documents accurately. How do we retrieve the right context?
steps.solution: Introduce a RAG Coordinator that embeds queries via Embedding Model, queries a Vector Candidates Index (e.g. Milvus/Pinecone), and injects top chunks into the LLM prompt.
tradeoffs: Dense embeddings miss exact keyword matches (e.g. error codes, product SKUs)
Chunk size trade-off: large chunks dilute signal; small chunks lose context
Vector search latency adds to overall time-to-first-token (TTFT)

steps.name: Ingestion Pipeline & Cross-Encoder Reranking
steps.interviewerPrompt: How do we continuously ingest thousands of changing documents, and filter out irrelevant vector search results?
steps.solution: Build an asynchronous document chunking and indexing pipeline, plus a Cross-Encoder Reranker before final prompt assembly.
tradeoffs: Two-stage retrieval: fast bi-encoder candidate selection + accurate cross-encoder reranking
Background ingestion indexing decoupled from query path
Output validation layer catches schema mismatches before sending to client

video-distribution.title: Global Video Streaming & CDN Architecture
video-distribution.subtitle: System Design Interview: Regional CDN POPs, Global Distribution, and Peer-Assisted Delivery

steps.name: Edge CDN POP & Origin Shield
steps.interviewerPrompt: Design a video streaming service where viewers stream HLS/DASH video chunks without overwhelming the storage origin.
steps.solution: Viewers fetch manifests, and video segments are routed through regional CDN POPs backed by an Origin Shield and storage cluster.
tradeoffs: Cache miss penalty: initial request for fresh chunks incurs high origin latency
Origin Shield protects primary database and S3 buckets from thundering herds
Bandwidth egress from single region remains costly for international viewers

steps.name: Multi-Region Global CDN
steps.interviewerPrompt: Traffic is scaling globally with spikes in East and West regions. How do we reduce cross-continent latency?
steps.solution: Deploy multi-region CDN edge POPs with geo-routed ingress and regional quotas, keeping 95%+ of traffic within local regional edges.
tradeoffs: Cache hit ratio depends on regional viewer density and content popularity
Quota limiting isolates regional traffic spikes and prevents rogue scrapers
Origin shield consolidates cross-region revalidations into single requests

steps.name: Peer-Assisted Hybrid Delivery
steps.interviewerPrompt: CDN egress costs are unsustainable during viral streams. Can viewers in the same region share segments directly without hurting buffering?
steps.solution: Introduce WebRTC peer-to-peer swarm mesh sharing for hot segments, with circuit breakers that fall back to CDN if peer transfer misses playback deadlines.
tradeoffs: Peer availability fluctuates dynamically; circuit breaker must detect stalls instantly
Slight CPU and upload bandwidth overhead on viewer devices
Offloads up to 60-80% of edge CDN egress bandwidth on popular live content

social-feed.title: Scalable Social Media News Feed
social-feed.subtitle: System Design Interview: Fan-out on Read vs Write, Timeline Caching & Graph Traversal

steps.name: Fan-out on Read (Naive MVP)
steps.interviewerPrompt: Design a basic social feed where users publish posts and read recent posts from people they follow.
steps.solution: Users publish posts to an admitted Posts DB. Feed generation queries the database on the fly by looking up followees and sorting their recent posts.
tradeoffs: Reading feeds requires joining users, follows, and posts on every page refresh
Read latency scales linearly with the number of followed users (O(N) queries)
Completely unfeasible for users following hundreds of people

steps.name: Fan-out on Write with Asynchronous Queues
steps.interviewerPrompt: How do we make feed loading instant (<20ms) for millions of readers?
steps.solution: Shift to Fan-out on Write: When a post is published, enqueue a background task. Fanout workers lookup followers and push the post ID into each follower's pre-computed in-memory Timeline.
tradeoffs: Timeline reads become instantaneous O(1) cache lookups
Celebrity problem: an account with 50M followers causes 50M writes on a single post
Hybrid approach needed: push for normal users, pull for high-follower celebrities

steps.name: Social Graph Service & Deadletter Handling
steps.interviewerPrompt: How do we handle billions of follow relationships with fast traversals, and what happens when timeline fanout workers crash?
steps.solution: Add a dedicated Graph Authority service for follower queries with retry protection, plus Dead-Letter Queues (DLQ) to isolate failing writes.
tradeoffs: Graph databases / distributed adjacency lists optimize follower lookups
DLQ prevents queue blockage from unprocessable fanout jobs
Hydration layer combines timeline post IDs with full post content in parallel
